questions.question:
**Direction: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.**

A. have seen a major blow

B. the last two years

C. people, and lower-income countries

D. to the world’s economy and

E. were hit particularly hard
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"BADCE". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• B. the last two years -
 
 
• This is establishing a timeframe within which something happened.
 
• This makes sense to start the sentence, so we know when the events occurred.
 
 
 
• A. have seen a major blow -
 
 
• This is stating the experience of whoever or whatever the sentence is about.
 
• "Have seen a major blow" means that they have been hit hard or badly affected by something.
 
• As it is phrased as an effect, it should follow a subject.
 
 
 
• D. to the world’s economy and -
 
 
• It seems to refer to the subjects that were negatively affected.
 
• This clause should precede A to establish what was affected.
 
 
 
• C. people and lower-income countries -
 
 
• This clause specifies other entities that have been affected.
 
• Ideally, it should come after the things that were affected were mentioned.
 
• Since D already mentions the world's economy, this clause completes the subjects which have seen the major blow.
 
 
 
• E. were hit particularly hard -
 
 
• This finishes the sentence by specifically focusing on how badly "people and lower-income countries" were affected.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the sentence correctly structured appears as follows:
 
 
• **The last two years have seen a major blow to the world’s economy and people, and lower-income countries were hit particularly hard.** 
 
 

So, the correct sequence is **"Option 3". **

questions.question:
**Direction: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

Were this boy / washing his clothes / yesterday when the matron / came for a regular round?
questions.solution:
Here, the erroneous part is **"Were this boy."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the part **"Were this boy."**
 
• The error is in the subject-verb agreement.
 
• According to the subject-verb agreement, a singular subject always takes a singular verb, and a plural subject takes a plural verb.
 
• The sentence should begin with **"Was" **instead of **"Were" **as the subject is singular (boy).
 
• The correct answer is Option 3.

 

**Correct sentence**: ***Was this boy**__ washing his clothes yesterday when the matron came for a regular round?*

__
 
• The error lies in the uniformity of the tenses.
 
• The sentence is in the past tense, so the correct verb form is the past simple.
 
• **"Had not call"** is the present perfect tense.
 
• **"Did not call"** is the correct past simple form of **"not call."**
 
• The correct answer is Option 2.

 

**Correct sentence**: *My parents **did not call**__ me yesterday.*

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the grammatically correct version of the following sentence.**

This phone is inferior of that one

options.text: This phone is inferior than that one.
This phone is more inferior than that one.
This phone is more inferior of that one.
This phone is inferior to that one.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"This phone is inferior to that one."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Inferior"** is a comparative adjective, so it needs to be followed by **"to"** when comparing two things.
 
• **"Than"** is used to make comparisons with adjectives that are not comparative, such as** "better" or "worse."**
 
• **"More inferior"** is redundant because** "inferior"** already implies a lower quality.
 
• **"Of"** is not the correct preposition to use when making comparisons.
 
• We always use comparative adjectives (like inferior) with **"than" or "to"** to show comparison.
 
 
• **Example**: *The performance of the new model is **inferior to**__ that of its predecessor in terms of speed and efficiency.*
 
 
 
• The correct answer is Option 4.

**Direction: Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice.**

Does she still love you?

options.text: Are you still loved by her?
Is she still loved by you?
Are you still loving by her?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Are you still loved by her?"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in active voice, where the subject "Basus" is performing the action of visiting.
 
• To convert it into passive voice, we need to make the object "you" the subject and add a form of "be" before the past participle "loved."
 
• The resulting sentence will have the object "her" after "by", indicating who performed the action.
 
• Also, the verb is placed before the subject in the Passive Voice.
 
• Structure:
 
 
• **Do/does + Subject + V1 + Object? (Active Voice)**
 
• Is/am/are + Object + V2 + by + Subject? (Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *Does Rahul love his parents?* (Active)
 
• *Are the parents loved by Rahul*? (Passive)
 
 
 
• The correct answer is Option 1.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: *Are you still loved by her?*
